angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 28,577,965 km at 69.98 pc = 5.46 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: distance 69.979 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.01), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 69.979 +/- 0.7 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 14.0910 +/- 0.4988 mas (same row, RUWE 3.26), 28.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 41.078 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: radius 41.078 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 733.504 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28,577,965 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4690 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: effective temperature 4690 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 3179: effective temperature 4690 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Cas: spectral type K0-IIIa (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Cas: projected rotation speed 8.5 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.06 from 2023ApJS..266...41P; the 17 published values span log g 1.12 to 2.71, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.7% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...41P)
